source.citation: Viúdez-Moreiras D., de la Torre Juárez M., Gómez-Elvira J., Lorenz R.D. et al. (2022), Winds at the Mars 2020 Landing Site. 2. Wind Variability and Turbulence, JGR Planets
source.dataset: Mars 2020 MEDA wind sensor at 1.5 m, mission sols <= 315 (MY36 Ls 22-153)
source.checked: values transcribed from the full text (Tables 1-2, sections 4-5); mean c*Gamma(1+1/k) checked against Table 2 in pipeline/tests/test_meda_winds.py

turbulence.definition: TI = standard deviation of wind speed / mean wind speed, over 10-min periods

notes: Dust devils move with the background wind (registry 3.1), so the relative speed variability of a moving hazard can be taken from TI: 36 +/- 10 % in daytime (the current storms.py assumption is 15 %).
TI is measured over 10-min windows at 1.5 m; the translation speed of a vortex averages over its size, so 36 % is an upper bound for its speed noise.
The paper gives no single number for wind-direction variability; it reports full wind rotations at 19-21 h LTST and strong direction disturbances during vortex passages.
